text_fidelity_a:
SHIMANO Stradic STCI4+4000FA Reel I love this reel. I have had mine for over two years maybe three and the only problem I have had is the bail trip spring mechanism recently started hanging. Opened it and cleaned it out and oiled it...no problems now. I caution about removing the bail covers. A spring and rod can come out and it took some doing to get it back in. I had to get the schematic from Shimano. The easiest way to re-assemble is to put the rod and spring in its place at the rear of the compartment replace the chrome cover and then insert the spring shaft into the bail housing in the hole provided. Then put the bail in place and put in the screw. Really no big deal but others not mechanically inclined may want to just send it off to have it completely cleaned.

This reel casts a mile due to the aero line wrap system that prevents line from becoming entrapped under other line. The retrieve and reeling is smooth as butter. The knob has bearing so there is no dragging whatsoever.

I fish this reel in salt and fresh water and have had no issues due to saltwater use. It is certified by Shimano to be saltwater safe.
I will be ordering my second one soon.
text_fidelity_b: SHIMANO Stradic STCI4+4000FA Reel

text_fidelity_a:
sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Electric Bike, 7-Speed Step-Through Touring Hybrid eBike, 26 Inch Wheels This review is for the sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Step-Through 500-Watt Electric Bike

The short version is: This is a great bike, sixthreezero has great support, and I highly recommend the bike and company.

My mom has some back issues, including fused vertebrae, and over the years, the number of physical activities she's able to participate in has declined. Long family bike rides on a normal bike were no longer an option. For that reason, in February we decided to go to a local Pedego store and rent e-bikes for my mom and wife. We did a 15 mile ride, and everyone, including my mom and wife, loved it.

My mom liked it so much that she reconfirmed the prices when we got back, but it was definitely outside of her budget.

We both spent the next several months looking for an e-bike deal that was too good to say no to. There's some cheap options online, a Costco mountain e-bike, some nice bikes that are out of our budget, both online and locally, but nothing that was amazing...

Until Prime Day 2019.

sixthreezero's 250-watt bikes were on sale during Prime Day. I don't even see them available now, but it was a great deal, and I did some research before phoning my mom and telling her I think we'd found the deal she was looking for. After telling my mom about it, she ordered one, then asked if I was getting one for my wife. I was on the fence, because it's still a lot of money, until she said, "Don't think about how much you're spending per ride. Do you want to have lots of happy memories of the family riding together or are you OK without those?"

Well said, Mom. I ordered one the next day.

Now, I don't see the 250-watt bikes on Amazon anymore, but when they were here, the online documentation, both here and over at sixthreezero at the time we ordered made the basic functionality seem the same between the 250-watt and the 500-watt bicycles. The key feature both my mom and wife were looking for was the ability to pedal with adjustable resistance, but leverage the throttle with the left thumb to accelerate with the motor when needed to either catch up quickly or tackle hills without issue. (And without changing the level of pedal assistance.)

Some of our first impressions were not great. My mom's bike showed up looking amazing, and my dad assembled it without issue, but the throttle did not behave as expected. (The boost was limited to the level of pedal assist you were in.) My wife's bike showed up, but the fender and rack were both badly bent.

Before buying the bike, I saw that sixthreezero, if you bought directly from them, was willing to offer 365 day test drives, and seemed really focused on customer satisfaction. The Amazon reviews seemed positive, and the box the bike came in offered free assembly at a local bike store. (I'm not sure how that works because I've built over a dozen bikes and this bike is easy to assemble.) That said, I had a damaged bike and it didn't perform as I was expecting. I was definitely concerned when I reached out to sixthreezero.

After multiple calls, photos and a video to confirm that my 250-watt bike did not perform the way their 500-watt did (the technician I was working with only had a 500-watt readily available to troubleshoot with), they were willing to work with my mom and I to find a satisfactory proposal that would allow us to send back the 250-watt bikes and they would ship us 500-watt versions.

They were polite and reasonable throughout the process, but I was still nervous about bike number two, since the first bike did arrive with issues outside of the e-bike functionality. I was pleasantly surprised that they seem to have people working there who seem to genuinely want to make sure their customers love their bikes.

The 500-watt bike went together very easily, and after assembling and tuning the bike, I took it for a ride. The bike was a blast.

The only thing that jumped out at me as being substantially different from the Pedego my wife rode was the seat post. The Pedego had a shock in the seat post, which doesn't do a lot, but is better than nothing. I ordered a "Sunlite Pillar Suspension Seat Post, 27.2 x 350mm, Silver" from Amazon, which seemed like a good improvement to the bike, which is otherwise fantastic. (The rigid seat post makes the ride a tad rough, which is why I gave comfort 4 stars, I'd bump that to 5 with the suspension seat post.)

My wife says she finds the sixthreezero 500-watt basically the same as the Pedego. I'm sure there are differences, but the only big one we see is the price.

I can't adequately describe an e-bike in words alone, but if you have the option to rent one locally, I highly suggest you try it. It's a lot of fun. I'm not a fan of skilled cyclists tearing up mountain bike trails with heavier, faster e-bikes, nor would I advocate road bikers throw electric motors on their bikes, but the joy e-bikes are able to bring families by leveling the field for families that want to ride together is awesome. And sixthreezero's EVRYjourney cruiser is a fantastic bike for those people.

We're averaging speeds of more than half a mile per hour more as a family than we used to, and my wife comes home with a smile on her face while my kids come home having used up more energy and me having gotten a better work out. I know this bike is not cheap, but I like the way my mom put it to me:

Would you rather be out riding with your loved ones? This is a fantastic option for those who can't match the speed or stamina of the people they're riding with.
text_fidelity_b: sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Electric Bike, 7-Speed Step-Through Touring Hybrid eBike, 26 Inch Wheels

Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.
text_fidelity_b: Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black

text_fidelity_a:
Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black This is a very well made tac light, very bright and compact. It uses a lithium battery which means it can sit around for years and still be ready when you need it. I like it, but there are a couple things to be aware of, especially for a tactical light, which means something that has to be 100% reliable and ready when you need it.

1) Hitting the mode you want is very tricky. You have to hit the switch just the right number of times (of course) and most tricky at just the right interval. The timing is VERY fast and it is different if you are going to use a particular mode temporarily (light press and hold button) or switching to that mode (press firmly and release staying on that mode). It takes practice, lots of it to hit the mode you want reliably.

2) When the battery runs out, there is absolutely NO WARNING. Either you will click it on and nothing happens or (most of the time) you will click it on and in a few seconds it goes dead. NOT a good situation for a tactical light. The only way this light can be absolutely ready for a critical situation is to put a new fresh $4 battery in it. Battery life isn't great, but that's the price for such a bright light running on a single CR123 battery. Just hope it is ready when you need it. A low battery indicator would be nice.

Still I gave it a soft 4 stars, maybe 3.5 would be more precise. It is a good light if you use it often enough to be good at hitting the right mode and if you have a fresh battery in it.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.
Here are the PROs:
- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.
text_fidelity_b: Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle

Northwest Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70" My niece is in her second year at Michigan, so my wife and I have been cheering for them. When I saw this Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70" (Michigan Wolverines - Blue,) I decided to grab it for when she visits and for around the house when we're watching football. So far we really like it, we are impressed, but we agreed, we cannot decide if it's deserving of 5 or 4 stars... here's why:

It arrived in a typical bag, so nicely folded and showing off the bright, brilliant colors. This was a plus. When opening it felt super soft instantly and we were thrilled. She's going to love it when she's here. My wife will love it for game days.

The material is great... but we cannot tell if it'll be one of those kinds that sheds or pills after (during) washing. We are not interested in washing it until it needs it, so we're not going to know until then. On the other hand, we shook it out and threw it a few times across the bed and shook it to try and see if something flew off - nothing did. So cool, all is well so far... Then why the continued concern? The stitching along the sides is average at best, really not great overall. For something we should be thrilled with, this weak spot was enough to not sooth our concerns. I try to show this in a couple pictures - all the way around you can see the batting sticking through - why is this and does this lessen the quality? Now you understand why we gave it the 5, but are giving the heads up on a possible 4.

The colors and design are wonderful - it looks great across the bed. And the reverse is just as nice looking. There is a "shadow" blue to the M which looks a bit... weird, but other than that - and it really doesn't dominate - it looks so cool.

So in the end we went with 5, we love the feel, my wife can't wait for cold weather, and my niece will love it ( and yea, don't say anything, but we'll likely get her one for Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Northwest Double Sided Cloud Soft Plush Throw Blanket 60"x70"

Gold's Gym XR 5.9 Weight Bench And that was just putting this bench together. Was given one of these as a Christmas present. But it was still in the box - so it had to assembled. From start to finish this took me more than an hour to do, and I built up a sweat doing it. This review is more about that experience as I haven't had the bench put together long enough to comment on how well it works for regular exercise.

First off, the model I got is a bit different than the one show in the photo on this product page. It's very similar, which leads me to think that there have been some recent design changes. The main differences I see comparing the photo to the one I got is that the two bars that rest on the floor are separate items that now attach with bolts instead of being welded. The only other thing I notice is that the pads on my bench are a solid color material, and not two -toned. There may be other differences but given the limited amount that I can see from the photo, that is all I can comment on.

You are going to need some tools to put this bench together. Number one on that list would be an [[ASIN:B000NIK9S2 adjustable wrench]] - you could probably use a socket wrench it you have a set. You also need at least a [[ASIN:B000NNFSKG wide mouth pliers]] - again you could use another adjustable wrench if you had one or even some regular slip-joint pliers. There are a lot of bolts & nuts that go into the assembly of this bench that need to be tightened. You're also going to need a philips-head screw driver. And in my case, I also needed a rat-tail file and a regular metal file.

Opening the box I was confronted with a lot of parts and pieces. Luckily the instruction were on top of all of that. Reading through them I found them pretty easy to understand and with the illustrations it was simple to follow the directions. All the hardware (nuts, bolts, washers, screws, and grease packet) was vacuum sealed to a piece of cardboard and everything was plainly labeled so that matching the right part to the directions was really easy. But be sure to read through the instructions before starting the assembly.

I found the bench fairly easy to assemble - but then I have had some previous experiences with doing this kind of thing. I would imagine some people might find the process a bit overwhelming. I did have one major hiccup. Step 5 has you connect the two parts of the frame (the bar that runs the length of the bench) together with two bolts. One piece of the frame slides into the other and you are suppose to line up to holes on one with the screw threads on the other. My pieces didn't line up. The holes didn't exactly match, so I could not get the bolts to screw in. I spent a half-hour with a rat-tail file trying to make one side of the holes larger, and then I got the bright idea to simply file down the end of the frame itself. That worked. If I hadn't been able to do that I would have had to return the bench and get a replacement. Once past that hurdle the rest of the bench was a snap to put together. I did think I had some 'spare parts' as I had a single nut and bolt left over when I was done - but reading through the directions again I found that I had missed putting those on the tip of the pivot bracket.

Now all I have to do is find the floor space to put this and time to use it. I'm giving this four-stars mainly due to the issue with the frame. I probably should give it an even lower rating because of that, but now that I have it all together it does look to be a decent piece of exercise equipment. I may later come back and update my review to comment on the use I'm getting out of it.

Review for Gold's Gym XR 5.9, model no. GCBE4869.8
text_fidelity_b: Gold's Gym XR 5.9 Weight Bench

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Beamer 5 Headlight I have owned the Beamer 5 from Planet Bike for 8 years. The same one. I can give it points for durability but not much else. Years ago I would have given it a higher rating but there are many better headlights today for the same or a little more money.

The first problem is that you just cannot make a bright LED light powered by only two AA batteries. Every small and cheap LED flashlight I've ever owned used 3 AAA batteries. Even when this light was a newer model there were flashlights of just about the same size with much brighter LED emitters and better optics in the same price range. Only thing lacking there was an integrated handlebar mount.

Don't be fooled by the number of LEDs. The number of LEDs has nothing to do with how bright a headlight or flashlight is. The LEDs in this headlight can be bought in bags of 100 for less than the cost of shipping. A single, more powerful LED is almost always better because you can build a better reflector around it with a more coherent beam of light.

In today's market, there are many headlights that offer better value for the money. There are a great many options with built-in lithium ion batteries offering longer run times and more power that aren't much more expensive. In this day and age I would only be looking at a headlight run on disposable batteries as an emergency backup for long rides when you're miles between outlets to plug a USB charger into.

Now, I've run this headlight through everything from torrential rain to blizzards and so far as I can recall it hasn't failed me. It just never put out very much light. The weather sealing is a simple O-ring which can wear out, but the light is designed in a way that even if a bit of water got in it wouldn't really get near the electrical contacts.

It is just barely bright enough to illuminate a clean, paved, and straight trail on a clear night. It doesn't have a wide enough beam to light around corners.

It's not bright enough in the fog to be noticed by drivers. In a winter environment with ice patches and chunks of slushy debris everywhere, it's dangerously dim. Rather than a nice smooth beam of light you can see dim lights in the beam from the lens. Don't forget about other riders wearing all black at night with no lights. Or people walking their dogs on 20 foot leases wearing all black on unlit trails.

Realistically the Beamer 5 is about as bright as a $5 LED flashlight from the bargain bin. Far and away more durable, but still dim.

I've just compared the Beamer 5 to the Light and Motion Urban 800 headlight and the difference was comical! Now, this is a $90 headlight, compared to a $30 one, but anything less than 100 bucks that makes me safer on the road at night is a good deal. Do NOT go cheap on your lights. Getting a bargain on a light is not worth your life, or even a minor injury.

Pros:
Decent handlebar mount
Well sealed
Durable
Quick and easy to remove from mount

Cons
Dangerously dim in many conditions
Narrow beam
Poor optics leave visible dim lines through beam
No battery level indicator
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Beamer 5 Headlight

text_fidelity_a:
Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit We do a lot of camping and living outdoors, and something we enjoy is easy to make food when we are outdoors. We look for ways to keep the cooler, extra stoves, skillets, dutch ovens and cast iron at home. I think we found our answer in Mountain House freeze dried entrees.

We purchased the Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit. In it we chose the Beef Stroganoff and took it to a scout meeting to try. During the scout meeting we talked about light weight backpacking as well as food options for emergency food at home.

After we boiled two cups of water we poured it into the pouch and zip locked it for 8 minutes. The contents where stirred and then served to many hungry scouts at the meeting. Every scout got a sample to try and a lot of them were hesitant. The overall surprise on their faces was priceless. They liked it and said it tasted great.

They wanted a pouch of the Beef Stroganoff for themselves. The scouts were surprised how easy the meal was to make and how simple the cleanup is. We did also like the zip lock feature not only for the re-hydrating process but also to keep the uneaten food for later if needed. They were also coming up with ways to reuse the pouch for other needs in the forest or on the trail to keep from throwing the empty pouch away.

Most of the scouts have never re-hydrated food or eaten MREs before. They were impressed with the ease of cooking and how lightweight it is to add to your day pack or back pack.

For camping, outings or emergency preparedness I would recommend Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit to have on hand. For one it has a long shelf life, for two you won’t starve as the contents of each pouch will satisfy a hungry kid or adult. A very tasty meal…especially in the middle of the forest!

Our only complaint (and the reason we deducted a star) is not all the water absorbed into the food, so it was very runny. The pack instructed to use 2 cups of water and I feel that was too much.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Just in Case 72 Hour Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Srixon Q-Star Tour 3 Golf Balls The long story:
A few weeks ago I hit a ball OB and found a Srixon Q-Star Tour that wasn't mine in the area. I dropped it and used it the rest of the round. Very soft feel, distance was good, and it spun the way I expected. I went back to my usual ball, which I like a lot and still like a lot, but every once in a while I'd pull that Srixon out the bag and play a hole of two with it. That soft feel just kept bringing me back to hitting it. Well, I lost it in a pond on a good shot - LOL! - that the wind pushed too far right. So, I decided to buy some on Amazon.

Jump to today and I used one of them on my weekly league round. Well I shot my best score of the season, putted, chipped, drove, everything was better than typical. On top of that, I used the same ball, literally the same one, for all shots on all 18 holes. Something I never seems to accomplish in the past.

Now I understand there are a lot of factors involved. Most of which fall on my shoulders. However, I'm really having a hard time going back to my old ball now. Even though I really like them.

So, bottom line, they may not give you the best round of the season, but they do preform as well as any ball I've played (better today). The price is half the super premium balls. I'd suggest trying them.
text_fidelity_b: Srixon Q-Star Tour 3 Golf Balls

text_fidelity_a:
Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.

text_fidelity_a:
Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike This is a low resistance exercise bike. The design is surprisingly solid, with one major problem: the belts are the wrong size!

This is why most people have torn belts in these things. Belt replacement is a major repair, requiring box/socket wrenches and allens, belt routing and careful tension adjustment and alignment.

The good news is that I figured out what belts do work in this thing:
4PJ610 (the wide belt, this is the same as OEM)
3PJ610 (the narrow belt, this is longer than OEM which was 3PJ584).
You can buy belts from Ametric, that's the only place I found.

You could probably get a shorter wide belt instead, but the combination above works pretty well - if tightened sufficiently, there is quite a bit of resistance in this bike.

The reason you want a longer narrow belt is because the tension adjustment is done on both belts at the same time, and the narrow belt is then overtightened and soon rips. Hope this helps you.

I also discarded all the plastic body parts, it's a naked bike now. After taking this thing apart twice, you'll want to do the same...

I sit on this bike when I work at my height-adjustable desk, sometimes all day.
text_fidelity_b: Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike

NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16 I am a Pittsburgh Steelers fan, so I admit that I just picked this cooler for the colors, and I don't even know the Missouri Tigers. But cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it!

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can put things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

I could have picked any of the NCAA teams that they make this cooler for, but I happened to pick the colors of my favorite pro football team, the Pittsburgh Steelers. (OK, I'm frugal and couldn't spring for the much more expensive Steelers cooler, but this way I get my team colors AND an awesome cooler.)
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Alta HR I came to this device from the Microsoft Band 2.0. So I was expecting a lack of functionality balanced by increased software support, community support and customization (bands).

This is a great minimal hardware design. Really like it. However software gates on cycling functionality (having to use your phone to start a “run” and convert it to a bike ride to see map data) are a bit annoying. If the user has turned on the connected GPS “feature,” why not just auto detect the bike ride AND show the map data when they're done?

The rotate wrist to turn on screen feature is accurate 50% of the time in real world usage. When you’re sitting at a desk or standing it is more like 90% accurate. When you are reclining on a couch, on your side, on your back, on your stomach, in bed, it does not work, at all. Get used to ensuring both arms are free so you can double tap the screen.

I purchased a braided metal band and the styling is great! I mean really nice compared to the Microsoft Band I owned previously. Almost elegant... I also like the professional look of the Alta HR with a black leather band.

After a week of use I would say that I probably should have purchased the Charge 2 HR or Charge 3 instead. They are also quite attractive, look good on a male wrist, and have significant additional functionality. Well I guess I"ll wait until the Charge 4 and hope it adds a GPS and returns to a chrome/brushed metal design similar to the Charge 2 HR (I’m not a fan of the finish options of the Charge 3).

East West U.S.A RTC530 Tactical Molle Attachment Smartphone Phone Holster If you get a good one this is a great phone holder. Unfortunately 2 out of the 4 holsters I got have major issues with how they were made. At first I thought it was just the way the case was laying but looking closer and comparing left and right sides I see stitches on each sides are in a slightly different position, causing the front part of the case to twist to the side. This also makes putting the phone in a more challenging, and the holster doesn't stay straight with the phone in it.

Other than the fatal flaw, some of the things it does well...

*Holds my phone with case. My phone is a bit taller than the default height for the case however the strap lengthens and will fit taller phones (with case my phone has exterior dimensions of 3 1/4" by 6 1/4" by 11/16")

*Has two "compartments" so I can carry something else with it (I don't think it will fit two phones the size of mine), and I can choose which to put my phone in (the outer one seems a bit slimmer than the inner.

*The female snap buckle is attached to the case so snapping in the closure strap is fairly easy one handed

*The lining on the inside means the phone is not exposed to the back side of fastener hardware.

Again, other than the major issues I had there are a couple ways it could be better...

*I'm not a fan of the open corners or the non-zippered top, because I feel that over time the phone and inside of the case may be exposed to dust and dirt which may scratch cheap phone screens. This shouldn't be a problem on better phones with better glass.

*Inside has a nylon webbing edging that catches on my phone case when my phone screen is facing out. This would be a big annoyance if I wanted to carry my phone that way.
text_fidelity_b: East West U.S.A RTC530 Tactical Molle Attachment Smartphone Phone Holster

On the negative side, I would like a stop/start function for steps and time, a stopwatch function, and an accumulative / total steps/miles display.

Accurate
Inexpensive
Easy to program

Cons:
No ability to start / stop step and time counter
No stopwatch
Must manually add steps/miles for each day to determine # of steps/miles achieved during week, month, etc.

Bottom Line: Works as advertised. Nothing more. Nothing less.

My husband built me a tetherball pole/base as the reviews on standard ones just didn't cut it. However, the base is not a concern in this review.

We've only played with the tetherball a total of 3 times. First time was fine (it was also the very first time my husband had actually played thetherball). But the second time when I played with a friend, the rope from the pole to the ball tore right at the base of the ball. I thought "no big deal I'll just tie it back on"

False. I tied it back on and within 30 minutes, it tore off again. I added on several knots and even went to YouTube to look up sturdy knots but that's not the issue. The string for this ball is VERY flimsy and weak.

On the third go around, the ball came flying off mid-serve and could have injured someone. Ball itself seems to be fine and sturdy. The rope itself, again, is just crappy overall. It keeps breaking and it's not easy to "re-string", if you will.

Overall, the ball is great and seems to be sturdy. However, if you're a grown adult looking into smacking the heck out of a tetherball, definitely be prepared to get a new, sturdier rope because the one that comes with it just doesn't cut it.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) My first Charge 2 was wonderful until it stopped reading my HR correctly after 5 months. My Charge 2 would tell me that my HR was 130+ when I was sitting or not even wearing it. On top of that, the wristband broke around the same time. I contacted support and they tried to fix the problem by having me restart my Fitbit however it did not work. Customer support was nice enough to offer me a replacement after going back and forth a few times.

Unfortunately the replacement Fitbit sent me was defective. I put the Fitbit on and tighten the wristband and position the Fitbit to the correct spot on my wrist but the Fitbit would not pickup my HR. After a few hours it started to read my HR however the reading was completely off. I took the Fitbit off and it continued to give me an outrageously high HR. It said my HR was 150 when I was just sitting or not wearing it. That's riduculous! I tried resetting the Fitbit many times but it did not solve the problem. I ended up wearing the Fitbit for a few months to see if it was just a one time fluke (I was also too lazy and feeling too frustrated to contact customer support AGAIN). Unfortunately the Charge 2 continued to read my heart rate incorrectly. To add onto the problem, this new Fitbit would think I'm walking when I'm just driving. I understand that most Fitbit will do this sometimes but mines was doing it all the time! No way I walked closed to 10000 steps each day. I've been lazy as F and I've been doing a lot of sitting these past few months LOL.

I finally found some free time today and hollered at customer service. They asked me to reset my Fitbit, so I did, but as I was doing so, my Fitbit battery suddenly drained and my Fitbit died. WHAT? After waiting for my Fitbit to come back to life the rep asked me to fire up the app and sync my Fitbit to the app. We tried 5 times and even reset the app but it didn't work. UGH this is now the FOUTH issue I'm having with this Charge 2. What a nightmare.

The rep quickly offered me a 50% discount for a new device or get my Fitbit Charge 2 replaced. NO WAY was I willing to get a THIRD Charge 2 and risk having to go through the headache of contacting customer service again if my THIRD Fitbit turns out to be defective too. I pestered the rep to see if she could give me a better discount, refund me, or give me credit to upgrade to a better model. Sadly, the rep and the supervisor did not have the power to offer me a better deal.

*When I asked for a refund or credit for a better model, the rep responded with this:

"I really understand your frustration Kimberly, however please be assured that our product team is constantly working to ensure that our products go through rigorous testing so that they can last and endure as expected."

LIES! Obviously Fitbit doesn't tell well enough if I've received two defective Charge 2.

*I asked if my warranty will be extended if I obtain a THIRD Charge 2:

Rep - If the device is out of warranty we will be unable to replace it and we may offer a discount to purchase a new device.
Rep - I understand your concern Kimberly, but if you decide to use the 50% discount to make a upgrade the new device will have a new warranty.
Rep - When you receive a replacement device, the replacement device has 30 days of warranty or the remaining of the original warranty.
Rep - So if the device fails which is not something that we expect to happen you have 30 days from the moment that the device is received in order to contact us again and get a replacement if necessary.

Sigh, this offer is not good enough. I wonder if I can sue for giving me a headache if my THIRD Fitbit also turns out to be defective...

*I then inquired about what happens if I have to claim a FOURTH Fitbit?

Me: would I qualify for a different model at that point
Me: or just another 50 % off discount
Rep: That would be a very unusual situation Kimberly and to answer your question, the amount of replacement devices that you receive does not makes you applicable for a free upgrade since that is a program that we don't have at the moment.
Me: Is it unusual that I received two fit bits that do not work
Me: Or is this fairly common
Rep: The reason is that the two devices that you have received failed in different areas Kimberly. Even this is not an expected situation.

Uh huh....

*Lastly, I asked if I will be sent a refurbished Charge 2 if I choose the replacement option:

Rep: Depending on available inventory, we sometimes issue factory-certified refurbished products as warranty replacements. These are typically products that were returned to Fitbit unused for reasons like wrong size and wrong color.
Me: Well that's not good
Rep: In most cases however, warranty replacements are brand new products that we package without accessories for easier shipping.
Me: how Do I guarantee that I get a NEW one
Rep: Since that depends on the warehouse Kimberly we have no control about if a new or factory-certified refurbished device will be sent.

I really wished Fitbit had a better buyer protection plan for unfortunate people like me. If you're reading this Fitbit, I would really like my money back or an upgrade to the Blaze or Ionic.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version)

text_fidelity_a:
StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires We loved the Rio Wonder Wheeler concept, but it didn't work so great in practice. When loaded, it was very difficult to pull over the sand. We then looked at higher-priced ones with balloon wheels, knowing that those would work better on soft sand. I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight Everyone knows the first rule: You get what you pay for. In this case though I think that you get more than what you expect. My experience so far is that this scope functions flawlessly. That has proven how well the Chinese can reverse engineer some products and manufacture them to relatively high standards. I would certainly be afraid to drop it but it is screwed together very well.

The second rule I abide by is: The more complicated the product, the more things that can go wrong with it. And this particular product has a lot of technical features. Think of it as a Swiss Army Knife but with battery powered components. It is actually designed quite well and looks good properly mounted but I doubt that it would continuously handle the recoil from a large caliber rifle or shotgun. However there is a 30 day "Money Back Satisfaction Guarantee" and a 12-month warranty if it goes bad.

The third rule that I usually follow is to buy at least one model higher (in price and quality) when I determine what I might need. In this case though it makes more sense to not get a more complicated scope/laser combo. Shooting/hunting is complicated enough depending on how your weapon functions, the conditions you're shooting under, and your ability to master the situation to end up successful. Typically the more things that can get in your way during a shooting situation can limit your results dramatically. So I always try to keep it simple.

This is a fun product however -- just make sure that you use it a lot during the initial 12 months. By then you will know what functions are most important to you, which weapon pairs with it the best (for you), and how dependable it is. Perhaps you only need a fixed blade knife instead of that Swiss Army Knife.
text_fidelity_b: UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender I've got a bicycle without any mounting holes for fenders. It also doesn't have enough clearance between the forks/brakes and tires to jerry-rig a fender. However, I hate not riding my bike because of light rain or a few puddles.

The Grunge Board was the best option that I could find at a reasonable price. It straps onto the downtube with a couple of rubber straps. I've got an 80s racing bike with tight geometry, and the dimensions of the board are small enough to clear the crankarms and the front wheel during turns. But just so (orientation makes a difference).

I've ridden through some big puddles and it seems to do a fairly good job of keeping my pant legs from getting soaked. I still put some scotch tape over the holes/slits around the bottom bracket to keep the gunk from getting in. The board is light enough that I leave it on all the time, even when it's not raining...just in case there is an unexpected puddle.

I have to take off a star because I think the mounting band should have been designed better. First, it hard to push the rubber bands through the narrow slots once they wrap around the downtube. The bands have slits in them that attach to nubs on the underside of the board. The nubs are not large enough to hold the bands in place perfectly securely. They seem to usually work, but the bands come off occasionally. If you have a small diameter downtube (as in most pre-90s, bikes), there are also a couple inches of extra rubber band that just flop around. It shouldn't be too hard for Planet Bike to redesign this retention mechanism, but it's also hard to complain for ~$10.

You can use a couple of cable ties instead of the rubber bands and they'd probably do a better job. You could also use a large soda bottle cut to size and get the same effect, though arguably a bit uglier.
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender

text_fidelity_a:
FDW Magnetic Bike Trainer Stand for Indoor Riding, Steel Bicycle Exercise Training Stand with Noise Reduction Wheel,Stationary Bike Resistance Trainer for Road & Mountain Bikes This stand is for bikes with NUTS not skewers and the plastic end caps are not necessary. I get better more secure mount without them.
This is a good stand for the money. The weather is wet and cold here and I used to hang my mountain bike up all winter. Here's what I have learned so far. The plastic caps that come on the axle mounts can shear right off if the axle does not protrude enough. One side of my axle stuck out a bit more than the other and the SHORT side was supporting all the weight on the plastic cap. It dropped off this morning and startled me a bit. I looked and saw the problem right away. I threw the mangled cap away and reset the axle after loosening the roller part. The metal to metal connection is much better and no harm comes to the bike nut or frame because only MILD torque is required to secure your bike axle. the weight is vertical, if you see the frame of the stand SPREAD at all you have over torqued! Just snug is fine. It's easy to move the tire to track in the middle of the roller, just loosen one side and then snug the other side till your tire is dead center. The roller tension is kind of by feel. If your tire is really inflated like mine you will need a bit of pressure to keep it from slipping, you can usually feel if the tire is slipping on the roller. Find a medium gear and stick with it, shifting gears is pointless and you'll run the roller to death on high gear anyway. The adjustment for roller resistance is a nice big knob that comes off and on with no tools. My street tires make almost no noise. If you are taking the bike off and on frequently. FIRST take the resistance knob off your handlebars and set it out of the way. SECOND take the roller pressure off so that it's free of the rear tire. THIRD remove the block riser from under the front tire or it will make it hard to get off the rear axle. FOURTH loosen the axle holders, it will help if another person can steady the bike while you do this but I did it by myself (this time). The riser block I got was a bit tall (3 inches) as a reviewer said the stand raised the rear wheel about 3 inches. That put me about 1/2 inch high in the front, but you don't want a lot of pressure on your hands anyway since you are stationary and not going anywhere. I found a short step stool helps me on and off the bike as it is now pretty high. Get on and off as carefully as you can. I will add more if needed to this review.
text_fidelity_b: FDW Magnetic Bike Trainer Stand for Indoor Riding, Steel Bicycle Exercise Training Stand with Noise Reduction Wheel,Stationary Bike Resistance Trainer for Road & Mountain Bikes

text_fidelity_a: Stanley GO The Quick Flip GO Bottle 24OZ Glass We have now owned several of these water bottles, as they are a really great size, and we enjoy the flip top feature; however, before purchasing, please know that the plastic lid has a weak point that will break if dropped on basically any surface at all.  While we try very hard not to drop our water bottles, accidents occasionally happen, and the lids of two of our water bottles are now broken.  I was hopeful that I could find replacement lids either on Amazon or on the Stanley website, but, evidently, they do not make replacement lids for these bottles.  I contacted the Stanley company just to make sure that they do not make a replacement lid (I explained that the lids were broken due to drops, and I was hoping to purchase new lids).  I received an email back stating that all Stanley products are covered under a lifetime warrant, and they then asked me to submit pictures and fill out a detailed form, which I did, though, it took me a long time to compile all of the requested information, and I had to resend the email 4 times as their email kept telling me that it was "undeliverable".  A few days later, I received an email saying that my "ticket" had been resolved and closed, but I had never received a response from my original email.  So, I emailed back stating that my issue was not resolved, and I resent all of the information that they had originally requested.  Weeks later, I received an email apologizing for how busy they are and stating that the warranty doesn't cover accidental damage, and that I should look on their website or Amazon for a replacement lid.  So, basically I just wasted a bunch of time submitting useless information that they never needed and never received an answer to my original questions.  So, that's that.  If you buy this water bottle, just know that if it gets dropped at all, the cheap, plastic lid will break, and you will be left with a very nice, but useless water bottle.

text_fidelity_a:
WWE Super Strikers Turnbuckle Takedown Ring This WWE Super Strikers Turnbuckle Takedown Ring is an item that I really thought, Oh No, another toy where I have to spend a fortune on buying the figures for this. I quickly found out that this is not the case at all. This ring fits all 6 inch figures, but you will need to at least buy one WWE Super Striker figure to be able to use the one launching turn buckle.

The ring is easy to put together and doesn't take long- we spent about 20 minutes. You are going to want to spend another $10.00 for one of the Super Striker figures, as launching a figure from the turn buckle platform is just way too much fun! I purchased John Cena, and the kids love him. His feet are different to fit on the launcher.

The scaffold can move or even collapse if hit that holds the chain that holds the champion belt. Also if the launched Super Striker figure flies into the Titantron screen- the screen can get smashed- and of course be put back together for more hits. You can also use the platform on the turn buckle to hurl an opponent into the ring. The platform attaches to any of the ring posts for more fun in trying to reach the belt hanging from the scaffold.

Any 6 inch figure can play in the ring and stand on the ropes. We already own the Mattel WWE Wrestling Champion collection of 4 six inch figures and they all play in the ring- they just don't have the feet with holes to fly off the launching turn buckle. I've seen every 6 inch figure we have in the house wrestle in this ring- wrestlers, older GI Joes, a 6 inch Harry Potter, even some 6 inch animals- especially a bear. This ring is a lot of fun for the kids- and you really only need to spend another ten bucks for a Super Striker figure that they'll love launching into the ring!
text_fidelity_b: WWE Super Strikers Turnbuckle Takedown Ring

And usually at the same time they zone into everything they shouldn't touch or have.  I remember my daughter at that age and tried my best to teach her to leave things alone...she would go after everything I said "no" to with that gleeful look in her eye!  Yeah, that's what this trampoline is for - they can bounce and bounce and bounce and get a LOT of that excess energy out of them without YOU having to chase after them or clear the room of anything they might get their hands on.  My friend has a covered back porch where we set this up and between the two of us, I think it took about 20 minutes.  It looks smaller in the picture than it seems when we put it up, but hey, that's a picture versus the actual item.  We sat down at the table to relax for a minute before her daughter brought over the little ball of energy that is her grandson.  Her daughter came out to see for herself and we all had a laugh when she put him in the trampoline enclosure.  At first he wasn't sure he liked it until he started bouncing and and squealing at the same time.  He was having a blast!  It's too bad he didn't have a brother or sister just a year or so older - they both would have had so much fun together!  But, the nice thing is, we had this set up outside, so he was getting his exercise in the fresh air, but in the shade so he didn't cook in the sun and we could sit nearby and sip ice tea and laugh and talk to him without having to chase him around.  Ah, that was the best part of having this trampoline - better than TV for watching and less strenuous than tearing around through the house after him for 3 hours before his internal battery winds down!

I wish I would have had these prior to surgery because the surgery didn't help! In fact, the surgery made me lose strength in my grip and I still get pain in my hands and forearms if I go a long period without using the handmaster system.
Using the Handmaster is the only way to release the pain and strengthen my hands and forearms. When I first started using these, the soft ball was almost too firm for my grip.
There are 9 muscles that open the hand and 9 muscles that close the hand and these exercise balls help increase circulation and strengthen these muscles.
The bands are tight, but they need to be because otherwise they would just roll down your fingers and wouldn't stay put through the exercises.
You can go to Doctor Zac's website (handmasterplus dot com) and there are videos to help you work out your hands and arms and education about how the muscles work.
These really work, but you need to give it time to work. After all, the problem didn't happen over night and it will not just go away.
I am in no way affiliated with Dr. Zac or this product, it just works.
text_fidelity_b: Handmaster Plus Physical Therapy Hand Exerciser - Finger Strengthener, Hand Therapy Balls for Exercise, Training - Finger Resistance Bands with Stress Relief Ball - Multicolored Balls, (9 Piece Set)

If someone asked me to recommend an air mattress, I would gleefully direct them to this one.

Assembly is a nightmare. I did some of it myself, but the front brakes were not making contact with the tire, so I got the help of my husband so we could make adjustments (he has some experience with mechanics). After about 30 minutes of adjusting the brake apparatus with no significant improvement, he decided to move the washer for the front brakes to the inner side just to give it a little more braking power by alleviating the gap between the brake and the tire—it was the only thing that worked. I also noticed that the bell on this bike doesn’t have an actual lever that you swing to the side to make a real bell ding—this one has a plastic bit that you hit and you hope it dings and reverberates off the metal circle it’s attached to—it’s not the best bike bell we’ve had.

It does look like a cute bike when everything is assembled, but it doesn’t seem as well constructed compared to our little 12 inch Minnie Mouse bike from Huffy. Strangely enough, some of the protective wrapping for this RoyalBaby bike said Huffy on it, so I’m not sure if this is a division of the larger parent company perhaps? I feel bad giving this 2 stars, but I honestly don’t think it’s spectacular for the money (probably a 3-star bike), but the assembly issues knocked it down to 2 stars, along with the poor instructions. I’ll be sure to buy a pre-assembled bike when we need the next size up.

Coleman Camping Tent | 6-Person Dark Room Dome Camping Tent with Fast Pitch Setup, Blue I am a Coleman fan. I have used many of their tents over the years. This one is just okay. I am mostly concerned with the false advertising. I think that's beneath them. This tent is NOT total dark room. It's only dark room tech in the upper portion. As you can see from the photo the lower half of the tent is just the regular tent fabric and the amount of light is very obvious, and this is in a dim basement. With that said, I can easily see having the upper portion dark could really help with people like me who love to camp but struggle with the amount of daylight that comes through in very early morning or at nap time, but it is NOT full dark room tech.

I am also very concerned about the "hub" connection at the top; maybe a great idea but seems very fragile to me. I think they would have been better off using decent, stronger poles, and keeping it a regular dome tent set up, which is a super easy style tent to set up. The poles seem weak. Make sure you have set each connection well into it's socket, and take set-up slow and easy.

The verdict is out whether I will keep this tent or not.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent | 6-Person Dark Room Dome Camping Tent with Fast Pitch Setup, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size Only the 2nd pair of snowshoes owned over the past +30 years. The old Sherpas are fine, but have been lusting over a pair of NorthernLites Backcountry for years. YOLO. Splurge. Outside of a significant weight savings, the binding system is nicer than the old Sherpas. Simple to put on or remove even with gloved hands. Only fiddling was tucking away the speed binding lace. Couple loops around the heel strap before tightening it.

Just in from the 4th hike. Logging an average of +9km per hike over rolling terrain in 6-12" of fresh light powder like snow. At 60kg these shoes are a bit on the too large size. Personal preference for 30"ers. The shoes track nice. Traction going up and down hill is good. Traversing a steeper face is a bit of an issue. No heel lift platform becomes an issue on longer, steeper climbs. Hit a short section of trail that was groomed for fat tire bikes. Real hard packed groomed. Shoe from some people trail runners left a minimal imprint. Left the snowshoes on for the couple hundred meters. Traction was excellent.

Expectations are for a durable product based on the past history of this brand of snowshoe.

Good for those looking for a light weight, easy on/off snowshoe for use in rolling terrain in fresh snow.
text_fidelity_b: RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light This is a very nice bike light/battery combo. With a simple twisting motion, you can turn it on, and then an additional slight twist runs it through 5 alternate modes - super bright, very bright, low light, strobe, occasional blink - and it lasts long enough at low light setting to last for some time.

A few caveats - if you plan on doing an extremely long night trip, you have to use a low-light setting, as the high power setting drains the battery quickly. At 3350 mAh, the battery doesn't last an extremely long time (I had about 25% charge left after 4 hours use at low setting), but it charges quickly, and for a combo device, it's not too heavy (it's also clearly meant to take a bit of a beating, so I'm sure that part of it's bulk is thicker than usual casing). I find the mounting bracket to be very secure, and it includes a rubber tightener in case you have a slim handlebar rack.

Overall, I'm quite pleased with this device. It offers exactly what I need, without being too excessively bulky.
text_fidelity_b: KNOG PWR Modular Bike Light - Device Charging, LED, Programmable Bicycle Light
